## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix mixed-case writes so callers can update an entry using any casing accepted by the cache’s case-insensitive lookup.

## Changes

The pull request adds `Cache.set`, raises the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds, and adds tests for round trips, expiration, and the default TTL constant.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Normalize keys in `Cache.set` — After `set("alpha", 1)` followed by `set("ALPHA", 2)`, `get("ALPHA")` still returns `1`. The setter stores a separate uppercase key, while the getter looks up the lowercase key. — Callers that vary key casing can serve an old value after refreshing it. — Fix: Store the key using `key.lower()` and extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip` to cover a mixed-case overwrite.

## Suggestions

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Expire entries at their deadline — When `Cache().set("alpha", 1)` runs at monotonic time `1000`, `get("alpha")` still returns `1` at `1300`. The setter records `1300` as the deadline, and `app/cache.py:21` evicts only when the clock is strictly past it. — A caller can receive stale data on the expiration tick. — Fix: Use `expires <= time.monotonic()` at `app/cache.py:21`.
- app/cache.py:8 — tests — Exercise the five-minute default through the cache — A default cache that expires entries after one second would still pass `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes`. That test reads `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` directly, and the expiration test supplies an explicit one-second TTL. — The suite can miss a regression that expires default entries minutes too early. — Fix: Extend `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` to exercise `Cache()` with a controlled clock.
